subject: ISL is back, Marchand goes freestyle & more
preheader: Plus: para-swimming world records, a coach story worth reading, and today's threshold set.
heroHeading: Good morning swimmers and happy Monday
heroTeaser: Leon Marchand may not stop at butterfly and IM -- there's real talk about him racing freestyle at LA28, and the implications are wild.
outroLine: That's the week in the water. Happy swimming,

workout.dateLabel: Mon, Aug 31 · Distance freestyle threshold in the pool, rotational core stability on land

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: A 3,050-yard aerobic threshold session built around sustained distance freestyle repeats that train your body to hold power deep into fatigue.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: A rotational power and anti-rotation stability workout targeting the core demands of freestyle and backstroke -- the kind of work that pays off at the wall.

newsItems.title: Marchand freestyle, ISL return, and a pro training shake-up
newsItems.body: Leon Marchand competing in freestyle at LA28 is now a genuine conversation -- and it is not the only big storyline brewing. US pros are reportedly seeking new training bases, and the International Swimming League is on its way back.

newsItems.title: More world records fall at Para Pan Pacs
newsItems.body: Day 2 of the 2026 Para Pan Pacific Championships in Walnut delivered two more World Records, adding to the pair that dropped on Day 1. A stack of American Records also went down, making it one of the more electric early-week performances of the year.

newsItems.title: One coach's honest take on motherhood and the pool deck
newsItems.body: Tracy Slusser is speaking openly about how swimming's coaching culture has historically forced women to choose between having a family and having a career. It is a candid, worthwhile read for anyone who cares about who is building this sport from the inside.

newsItems.title: Olympian Josh Matheny leaves Indiana, weighs his options
newsItems.body: Josh Matheny, who competed at the 2024 Olympics, has announced he is departing Indiana and will spend the coming weeks talking with teams across the country. He is looking for a training environment that fits his next two years.

athlete.name: Kristof Milak
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: Martin Rulsch , Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Kristóf Milák is a Hungarian professional swimmer, born on 20 February 2000. He competes primarily in butterfly events and has established himself as one of the world's leading swimmers in the discipline, holding the world record in the long course 200 metre butterfly and the European record in the long course 100 metre butterfly.

At the 2020 Summer Olympics, Milák won gold in the 200 metre butterfly and silver in the 100 metre butterfly. He has won three gold medals and one silver at the World Aquatics Championships, three gold medals at the European Aquatics Championships, and three gold medals at the 2018 Summer Youth Olympics.
